chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Yahya al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you give the call to prayer (adhan) in open land and then establish the call (iqamah), two rows of angels pray behind you; and if you establish (the call) but do not give the call, one row of angels prays behind you."

key_terms.أَذَّنْتَ: You give the call to prayer (Adhan)
key_terms.أَقَمْتَ: You establish the call to prayer (Iqamah)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in angelic reward between giving adhan and iqamah versus only giving iqamah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the metaphysical presence of angels during the ritual call to prayer, specifically contrasting the spiritual magnitude of performing both adhan and iqamah versus only iqamah. In Shia scholarly tradition, this underscores the adhan not merely as a notification but as a significant act of worship that invites celestial witnesses, thereby enhancing the worshipper's connection with the divine realm. The distinction between 'open land' (ard fa'la) and other settings further emphasizes the public declaration of faith as a catalyst for this angelic accompaniment.
